title: A permanent capability lab for tiny language models
description: Three new lab addresses cover the tiny-model index with its capability matrix, the methodology page, and per-model verdict pages, linked from the footer and listed in the sitemap with no new scripts.
lead: The site now publishes a permanent lab for tiny language models: a fixed six-task battery with a shared rubric, a matrix comparing every evaluated model, per-model verdict pages with limits and reproduction notes, plus a backlog and a weekly routine. The footer carries the new link while the header stays unchanged.
merge_note: Pre-merge: this entry ships in the same change per the standing rule; the pull request number and merge identifier are recorded after the gate passes on the exact head.

stages.rationale: Verified the remote and login, then branched from the fresh main line.
Added the three lab templates with builder routes, footer link, sitemap coverage, and styles.
Opened the pull request with the lab pages and the log entry.
Merged the main-line data routes into the lab branch, combined the sitemap entries, footer navigation and artifact cap, and regenerated the output from source.

reasoning.DEV: The lab reuses the established static page pattern with no new scripts or page-level scrolling, using the article table idiom for the matrix with scoped headers and a labelled scroll region. The three templates, the builder routes, the footer link, the sitemap entries, and the additive token-bound styles ship together with this log entry. The deterministic build and the full test suite pass on the change with the artifact weight cap raised one step to cover the additive lab rules.
reasoning.SEC: Not evidenced in the linked record. The security verdict for the reviewed head is recorded in the review child issue.
reasoning.QA: Not evidenced in the linked record. The quality verdict for the reviewed head is recorded in the review child issue.
reasoning.Director: This change adds the lab through the existing page system with no visual or structural change elsewhere. Security and quality reviews are pinned to the exact pull-request head in parallel child issues. Release approval fires only when both verdicts pass that exact head.
